Mirror Trading Int. Bitcoin Scam

By: Sasha Schwendenwein | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We find out how the biggest ponzi scheme between 6-9 billion rands worked, and confront those responsible.

Unique Selling Point:
We have a more personalized approach in that we are interviewing Jan Vermeulen, whose life was turned upside down by the directors of Mirror Trading International - a bitcoin money making scheme that was actually a scam. In mid-to-late last year MTI's site was hacked and exposed by Anonymous ZA, proving what Vermeulen had been writing about for a long time, that the same directors - Cheri Marks/Ward and Clynton Marks (from a previous ponzi scheme BTI global) were doing it again - this time with MTI - whose CEO and founder is Johann Steynberg. After Vermeulen exposed them, they went after him and mybradband where it was published, and they went on the defensive putting out many videos etc insisting that it was not a scam and people should not take their money out. Then in November, based on the hack and information from sources, FSCA's Brandon Topham's team went in and executed an Anton Piller order the business address in Polokwane, and the Marks' home in Durban. Since then the scheme has collapsed, despite the best of efforts by the Marks'. And Steynberg has left his wife and gone on the run.

Summary:
We would interview case studies - we have over 50 to choose from (before december) and more from vermeulene etc... We would interview the lead advocate Vaughn vcitor about how the case is unfolding and put in a request to the hawks. We'd also also the FSCA's Brandon Topham. And we can interview anonymous ZA.

Then we'll go after clynton and cheri who are really the ones that are responsible for BTC global. We have some nice extra information on both of them, great videos etc, and we'll have to put a right of reply in to Steynberg, and potentially his wife Nerina - who is a manager at the polokwane pick n pay.

Further information:
A hacker collective calling itself Anonymous ZA has released explosive details about Mirror Trading International (MTI), stating that at least R4-billion in bitcoin has flowed through the scheme.

In response, MTI told MyBroadband the information stems from private member data that was illegally obtained and that it is “inaccurate at best”.

Mirror Trading International is a South African registered company offering Forex trading services by using an automated system to trade with the trading pool on behalf of its members.

Johann Steynberg is the CEO and founder of MTI, which focuses on Bitcoin trading and promising members a “truly passive income”.

According to MTI, it has over 90 000 active members in 177 countries, and its numbers are growing daily.

MTI made headlines recently after the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) said it was investigating the company.

The FSCA said the current business model of MTI requires it to be in possession of a financial service provider licence.

“MTI has informed us that they accept clients’ funds in the form of Bitcoin, pool the funds into one trading account on a forex derivate trading platform, and conduct high-frequency trading through the utilisation of a bot,” the FSCA said.

If this is being done as described, then this amounts to financial services, hence the licence requirement.

However, the FSCA has a much greater concern about MTI’s activities.

The company claims to have more than R2.9 billion in clients’ funds in trading accounts, but the FSCA has not been able to conclusively confirm that the funds exist.

“Moreover, the returns on the investments claimed by MTI seems far-fetched and unrealistic,” the FSCA said.

At the time, MTI said that its bot-trading is able to generate consistent profits of an average of 10% per month. More recently it said it has seen an average return of 0.5% per day.

The FSCA recommended that MTI clients request refunds into their own accounts as soon as possible.

The Texas State Securities Board has also issued an emergency cease-and-desist order against MTI and accused it of perpetrating fraud through an illegal international multilevel marketing programme.

Canada’s Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) has placed MTI on its list of illegal online platforms, issuing a warning that MTI illegally solicits investors.

Anonymous ZA publishes information about MTI
Anonymous ZA has published financial information about MTI online based on data collected through MTI’s members portal – mymticlub.com.

According to Anonymous ZA, it discovered glaring security vulnerabilities in the online systems of MTI, which it exploited to extract information about the inner workings of the scheme.

Anonymous ZA said the vulnerability that exposed MTI’s “back office” system was a lack of basic authentication.

Any registered member who is logged into the system could view the information of any other member’s account by simply changing a parameter in the URL.

“All data was acquired using simple enumeration and scraping techniques on the mymticlub.com site,” stated Anonymous ZA.


“No hacks were performed because the lack of basic security did not require it. Just incrementing an id=? parameter on various URLs provided all the data that you see here.”

Using this weakness, it was able to glean detailed information about MTI’s system and see the full names, usernames, e-mail addresses, bitcoin balances, and earnings linked to every account.

Anonymous ZA then published an anonymised copy of the data, which was current as of 14 September 2020, on a dark web site called MTILeaks.

It said the MTI database shows the company has handled over 22,984 bitcoin in member deposits, amounting to over R4 billion.

The data shows that members have withdrawn nearly 15,653 bitcoin (close to R2.9 billion), which means the scheme should still have at least 7,331 bitcoin (over R1.3 billion) of members’ capital in its accounts.

However, the data also shows that the scheme has allocated almost 9,916 bitcoin (over R1.8 billion) to members in interest and bonuses.

This means that MTI must have a minimum of 17,247 bitcoin (over R3.1 billion) to cover the remaining deposits and earnings of all members who have not yet been withdrawn from the scheme.

MyBroadband asked MTI CEO Johann Steynberg if the company has that much liquidity and if he could provide MTI’s bitcoin wallet addresses to prove that the company has the assets to cover its obligations.

Steynberg did not answer the question in his initial response to MyBroadband.

In a subsequent statement to MyBroadband, MTI said it declined to comment.

two day shoot
Potentially 4 days edit as it will be graphics intensive with floris. and potentially 12 minutes if possible as we have a lot of history and technical history to get through.

Script:


Over the past three years we’ve received nearly 200 submissions on Crypto currency scams alone.
MANY OF THESE ARE MULTI LEVEL MARKETING OR MLM SCHEMES. THESE REQUIRE MEMBERS TO RECRUIT MORE MEMBERS IN ORDER TO GAIN A REFERRAL BONUS. ACCORDING TO THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, IN ORDER FOR AN MLM TO BE LEGAL, THEY MUST SELL A PRODUCT OR OFFER A SERVICE.
“MTI SO MUCH MONEY SO MUCH MONEY… ROCKET…
Mirror trading international or MTI began in 2019 in Stellenbosch and claims to have 280,000 members world wide, with roughly 9 billion rands worth of investments. This is their sales pitch:
FOR JUST 100 TO 200 DOLLARS YOU TOO CAN INVEST. BY USING ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE TECHNOLOGY IN THE FORM OF A BOT THEY’LL TRADE YOUR INVESTED BITCOIN IN ORDER TO GAIN OBSCENE PROFITS - RANGING FROM 10% PER MONTH TO HALF A PERCENT PER DAY.
Cheri: With MTI you have an opportunity to grow the number of bitcoin you have, each day your bitcoin will grow with the profits added from trading.
Chante: We had a little money lying in the bank, you know everybody is talking about this MTI.
Chante Hughes is a single mother, in November 2020 she invested around R40,000.
The first two payouts was good it was R7000, it was nice to convince me, listen this is legit, and it’s a south african guy.
That South African guy is CEO Johann Steynberg. A businessman whose history is littered with various unsuccessful MLM schemes.
Steynberg: We do not need new members’ funds, to deliver on our brand promise...MTI is clear on their mission, and that is helping ppl to grow bitcoin through our training services.
The head of MTIs referral and Members program is former Mr Johannesburg Clynton Marks...His wife Cheri Marks headed up MTI communications.
Chante: She was one of those guys she can sell you snow in the summer.”
All seemed well to Hughes until all withdrawals stopped in mid-December.
Chante: Just the payout before Christmas Eve, I never received. We should have got out about 70000 already.
To investor’s horror Steynberg may have done a runner.
MTI RELEASED A BIZARRE STATEMENT, THAT BEFORE DISAPPEARING STEYNBERG ALLEGEDLY RECEIVED A WARNING THAT HIS LIFE WAS IN DANGER, AND HAD FLED TO BRAZIL AFTER WHICH ALL COMMUNICATIONS CEASED. BUT ‘WHERE IS THE MONEY?’ ACCORDING TO MTI IT’S STUCK IN THEIR “UNREGULATED BROKER’S” ACCOUNT - THE MYSTERIOUS TRADE300.
But a group of hackers - Kid Colt, Pedro and Mr Original under the banner of Anonymous South Africa - had seen this coming. In September they delved behind MTIs website and leaked evidence allegedly revealing it to be a scam.
MO: it's a group of loosely affiliated individuals that have varying technical skills that try to achieve a common goal in the public interest
P: The members were owned about 17000 Bitcoin and the scheme only had 7000 Bitcoin in it. Clynton Marks was at the top of the binary tree, not Steynberg. Each of those top individuals on average withdrew between R200-R30 million.
Jan: In fact, Clynton Marks is a 50% shareholder.
Award winning investigative journalist Jan Vermeulen operates in the tech space. He reported on this story for Mybroadband. Initially MTI traded Forex.
Jan: When they landed in hot water with a financial sector conduct authority, they changed to trading cryptocurrencies because they believed that they could skirt South African regulation, and they switched to using this legendary AI.
THIS IS HOW A MULTI LEVEL MARKING SCHEME WORKS - IMAGINE YOU RECRUIT 5 PEOPLE, AND THOSE PEOPLE RECRUIT 5 PEOPLE AND SO ON… IT TAKES ABOUT 14 ITERATIONS OF EACH PERSON RECRUITING JUST 5 PEOPLE BEFORE THE WHOLE WORLD'S POPULATION IS RECRUITING. THESE SCHEMES ARE INHERENTLY UNSUSTAINABLE.
And it’s that unsustainability that caught the attention of the Financial sector Conduct Authority or FSCAs Director of Investigations Brandon Topham.
BT: The FSCA is a primary objective to protect the public from investors, financial institutions, ripping them off. It was a WhatsApp group that I’m in, and someone was recruiting. And I said, guys, I can tell you now, this is not legit. I opened up the case internally.
Jan: Imagine Investec or Coronation telling you that a proportion of your earnings, let's say 30% of the earnings of your investment in their fund is locked behind recruiting people into the scheme. people will pull the money out of those funds overnight.
Cheri Marks says it is a legal Multilevel Marketing Scheme...
Cheri: Obviously i get the questions is MTI a ponzi scheme all the time…everybody seems to think that anything that has a recruiting function or a referral function is a pyramid scheme, its not, guys when you are asking questions like that then you don’t actually now what you’re talking about you look a little silly i must be honest…if your company does not have a service or product attached to it then you’ve got a problem...
The FSCA did believe MTI had a problem, so Steynberg and Cheri Marks went to the FSCA to give THE REGULATORS a demonstration of the bot doing live trades.
Topham: there's no such thing as a magical computer. There's no trading platform whatsoever that we could find. It was basically his own trading platform that he was demonstrating, I said but that's derivative trading. He said, what’s a derivative?
A derivative’s value is based on the underlying asset, like bitcoin, and fluctuates according to the asset's expected future price.
Chante: It was very convincing because, there is really a Bitcoin machine that they say it works the whole time, going with the American dollar and stuff.
BT: Warren Buffett said, if you don't understand it, stay away from it.
AND THE FIRST THING YOU NEED TO UNDERSTAND ABOUT BITCOIN IS THAT THERE WILL ONLY BE 21 MILLION COINS MINTED. FROM THAT FACT, VERMEULEN WORKED IT OUT MTIs SCHEME WOULD HAVE THEM OWN ALL THE BITCOIN IN THE WORLD WITHIN 2- 5 YEARS, DEPENDING ON THE VARIABLES.
Jan: To explain Bitcoin in a nutshell, it is a digital currency, and a banking system, when no one has to trust one another and where there's no central authority. Bitcoin is worth over 600,000 rand per coin.
This led MTI leadership to splurge.
Kid Colt: The guys who got in first all bought themselves new cars, fancy cars, they bought new houses.
Including the Marks’ who allegedly live in this 11 million rand home.
Pedro: the house is not actually owned by them, they've obviously set up their assets in such a way that it would be difficult to liquidate. This shows foresight on their behalf.
In writing the Marks say there’s nothing sinister about living in a friends house.
Cheri: We are annoyed that ppl think they can behave criminally in a way that is unbecoming, and that they can publish this information that is not verified or factually inaccurate.
Jan: Many of the people involved in MTI have been involved in a previous scam. The FSCA, they actually issued a warning back in August.
Then in November the FSCA raided MTI.
Cheri: They believe that if they take our laptops and our phones they’ll find proof of MTI being illegal, but the truth is they are going to find proof of trade which ‘we’ve already given then, and bitcoin balances’.
But then the FSCA found out Trade300 - their broker - was a front.
Claire: What about trade 300?
Topham: Our infestation into this broker trade 300, led us to a website, which is owned by the CEO of MTI.
In this leaked zoom video from December, Cheri Marks reports this to leadership.
CM: what to say to ppl? That johan has scammed all of us and run away with out bitcoin, i can’t say that. I’ve got irrefutable proof that johann created trade 300, we all bought into his vision, now to find out that that man has lied to us…Johann was the CEO, he was the person who ran everything.
In writing the Marks’ say they aren’t traders, and therefore never doubted the authenticity of the trades. However, any funds they've utilized are proceeds of trades outside of MTI.
Cheri: Clynton has over 500 bitcoin in MTI every cent my family has is in MTI... Clynton and I had nothing to do with the situation.
Clynton says he is not a director, and contradicted his wife’s claim, denying he invested 500 bitcoin.
KC: These leaders are now all saying, we didn't know. We're not technical. They blatantly have taken money from people. They knew and they need to face the consequences.
But many suspect Steynberg is a puppet, and there’s a puppet master operating MTI’s strings behind the scenes.
Mr Original: from the start Steynberg was going to be the fall guy and vanish off into the sunset.
Steynberg hasn’t responded to multiple requests for comment, but the Hawks are investigating, and this week the court appointed provisional liquidators.
BT: Don't spend the money. So if you made a perfectly legitimate investment of fifty thousand rand, you got back seventy thousand rand. In terms of the law, they can ask for the whole seventy thousand rand back. You will have a claim for your fifty thousand with every other investor.
Enter Advocate Vaughn Victor whose team has been tasked by the liquidators to track down the bitcoin.
Vaughn: We know where most of it is. But its a difficult process because some of the members laundered the money to obscure the origin of these transactions.
Claire: You’re saying it’s not 280,000 investors?
Its 48-60,000 investors. Because there was a doubling of accounts, one member had 100 accounts. the root of evil is not money. It’s the love of money.
Chante: I lost money. I'm disappointed in myself, my son is disappointed to me. I don't want to see other people end up losing everything
BT: don't expect to get the money next month or next year. If you're lucky you might get a small percentage back.

Cheri: With MTI you have an opportunity to grow the number of bitcoin you have, each day your bitcoin will grow with the profits added from trading. Chante: We had a little money lying in the bank, you know everybody is talking about this MTI. Chante Hughes is a single mother, in November 2020 she invested around R40,000. The first two payouts was good it was R7000, it was nice to convince me, listen this is legit, and it’s a south african guy. That South African guy is CEO Johann Steynberg. A businessman whose history is littered with various unsuccessful MLM schemes. Steynberg: We do not need new members’ funds, to deliver on our brand promise...MTI is clear on their mission, and that is helping ppl to grow bitcoin through our training services. The head of MTIs referral and Members program is former Mr Johannesburg Clynton Marks...His wife Cheri Marks headed up MTI communications. Chante: She was one of those guys she can sell you snow in the summer.” All seemed well to Hughes until all withdrawals stopped in mid-December. Chante: Just the payout before Christmas Eve, I never received. We should have got out about 70000 already. To investor’s horror Steynberg may have done a runner. MTI RELEASED A BIZARRE STATEMENT, THAT BEFORE DISAPPEARING STEYNBERG ALLEGEDLY RECEIVED A WARNING THAT HIS LIFE WAS IN DANGER, AND HAD FLED TO BRAZIL AFTER WHICH ALL COMMUNICATIONS CEASED. BUT ‘WHERE IS THE MONEY?’ ACCORDING TO MTI IT’S STUCK IN THEIR “UNREGULATED BROKER’S” ACCOUNT - THE MYSTERIOUS TRADE300. But a group of hackers - Kid Colt, Pedro and Mr Original under the banner of Anonymous South Africa - had seen this coming. In September they delved behind MTIs website and leaked evidence allegedly revealing it to be a scam. MO: it's a group of loosely affiliated individuals that have varying technical skills that try to achieve a common goal in the public interest P: The members were owned about 17000 Bitcoin and the scheme only had 7000 Bitcoin in it. Clynton Marks was at the top of the binary tree, not Steynberg. Each of those top individuals on average withdrew between R200-R30 million. Jan: In fact, Clynton Marks is a 50% shareholder. Award winning investigative journalist Jan Vermeulen operates in the tech space. He reported on this story for Mybroadband. Initially MTI traded Forex. Jan: When they landed in hot water with a financial sector conduct authority, they changed to trading cryptocurrencies because they believed that they could skirt South African regulation, and they switched to using this legendary AI. THIS IS HOW A MULTI LEVEL MARKING SCHEME WORKS - IMAGINE YOU RECRUIT 5 PEOPLE, AND THOSE PEOPLE RECRUIT 5 PEOPLE AND SO ON… IT TAKES ABOUT 14 ITERATIONS OF EACH PERSON RECRUITING JUST 5 PEOPLE BEFORE THE WHOLE WORLD'S POPULATION IS RECRUITING. THESE SCHEMES ARE INHERENTLY UNSUSTAINABLE. And it’s that unsustainability that caught the attention of the Financial sector Conduct Authority or FSCAs Director of Investigations Brandon Topham. BT: The FSCA is a primary objective to protect the public from investors, financial institutions, ripping them off. It was a WhatsApp group that I’m in, and someone was recruiting. And I said, guys, I can tell you now, this is not legit. I opened up the case internally. Jan: Imagine Investec or Coronation telling you that a proportion of your earnings, let's say 30% of the earnings of your investment in their fund is locked behind recruiting people into the scheme. people will pull the money out of those funds overnight. Cheri Marks says it is a legal Multilevel Marketing Scheme... Cheri: Obviously i get the questions is MTI a ponzi scheme all the time…everybody seems to think that anything that has a recruiting function or a referral function is a pyramid scheme, its not, guys when you are asking questions like that then you don’t actually now what you’re talking about you look a little silly i must be honest…if your company does not have a service or product attached to it then you’ve got a problem... The FSCA did believe MTI had a problem, so Steynberg and Cheri Marks went to the FSCA to give THE REGULATORS a demonstration of the bot doing live trades. Topham: there's no such thing as a magical computer. There's no trading platform whatsoever that we could find. It was basically his own trading platform that he was demonstrating, I said but that's derivative trading. He said, what’s a derivative? A derivative’s value is based on the underlying asset, like bitcoin, and fluctuates according to the asset's expected future price. Chante: It was very convincing because, there is really a Bitcoin machine that they say it works the whole time, going with the American dollar and stuff. BT: Warren Buffett said, if you don't understand it, stay away from it. AND THE FIRST THING YOU NEED TO UNDERSTAND ABOUT BITCOIN IS THAT THERE WILL ONLY BE 21 MILLION COINS MINTED. FROM THAT FACT, VERMEULEN WORKED IT OUT MTIs SCHEME WOULD HAVE THEM OWN ALL THE BITCOIN IN THE WORLD WITHIN 2- 5 YEARS, DEPENDING ON THE VARIABLES. Jan: To explain Bitcoin in a nutshell, it is a digital currency, and a banking system, when no one has to trust one another and where there's no central authority. Bitcoin is worth over 600,000 rand per coin. This led MTI leadership to splurge. Kid Colt: The guys who got in first all bought themselves new cars, fancy cars, they bought new houses. Including the Marks’ who allegedly live in this 11 million rand home. Pedro: the house is not actually owned by them, they've obviously set up their assets in such a way that it would be difficult to liquidate. This shows foresight on their behalf. In writing the Marks say there’s nothing sinister about living in a friends house. Cheri: We are annoyed that ppl think they can behave criminally in a way that is unbecoming, and that they can publish this information that is not verified or factually inaccurate. Jan: Many of the people involved in MTI have been involved in a previous scam. The FSCA, they actually issued a warning back in August. Then in November the FSCA raided MTI. Cheri: They believe that if they take our laptops and our phones they’ll find proof of MTI being illegal, but the truth is they are going to find proof of trade which ‘we’ve already given then, and bitcoin balances’. But then the FSCA found out Trade300 - their broker - was a front. Claire: What about trade 300? Topham: Our infestation into this broker trade 300, led us to a website, which is owned by the CEO of MTI. In this leaked zoom video from December, Cheri Marks reports this to leadership. CM: what to say to ppl? That johan has scammed all of us and run away with out bitcoin, i can’t say that. I’ve got irrefutable proof that johann created trade 300, we all bought into his vision, now to find out that that man has lied to us…Johann was the CEO, he was the person who ran everything. In writing the Marks’ say they aren’t traders, and therefore never doubted the authenticity of the trades. However, any funds they've utilized are proceeds of trades outside of MTI. Cheri: Clynton has over 500 bitcoin in MTI every cent my family has is in MTI... Clynton and I had nothing to do with the situation. Clynton says he is not a director, and contradicted his wife’s claim, denying he invested 500 bitcoin. KC: These leaders are now all saying, we didn't know. We're not technical. They blatantly have taken money from people. They knew and they need to face the consequences. But many suspect Steynberg is a puppet, and there’s a puppet master operating MTI’s strings behind the scenes. Mr Original: from the start Steynberg was going to be the fall guy and vanish off into the sunset. Steynberg hasn’t responded to multiple requests for comment, but the Hawks are investigating, and this week the court appointed provisional liquidators. BT: Don't spend the money. So if you made a perfectly legitimate investment of fifty thousand rand, you got back seventy thousand rand. In terms of the law, they can ask for the whole seventy thousand rand back. You will have a claim for your fifty thousand with every other investor. Enter Advocate Vaughn Victor whose team has been tasked by the liquidators to track down the bitcoin. Vaughn: We know where most of it is. But its a difficult process because some of the members laundered the money to obscure the origin of these transactions. Claire: You’re saying it’s not 280,000 investors? Its 48-60,000 investors. Because there was a doubling of accounts, one member had 100 accounts. the root of evil is not money. It’s the love of money. Chante: I lost money. I'm disappointed in myself, my son is disappointed to me. I don't want to see other people end up losing everything BT: don't expect to get the money next month or next year. If you're lucky you might get a small percentage back.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): We find out how the biggest ponzi scheme between 6-9 billion rands worked, and confront those responsible.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: We have a more personalized approach in that we are interviewing Jan Vermeulen, whose life was turned upside down by the directors of Mirror Trading International - a bitcoin money making scheme that was actually a scam. In mid-to-late last year MTI's site was hacked and exposed by Anonymous ZA, proving what Vermeulen had been writing about for a long time, that the same directors - Cheri Marks/Ward and Clynton Marks (from a previous ponzi scheme BTI global) were doing it again - this time with MTI - whose CEO and founder is Johann Steynberg. After Vermeulen exposed them, they went after him and mybradband where it was published, and they went on the defensive putting out many videos etc insisting that it was not a scam and people should not take their money out. Then in November, based on the hack and information from sources, FSCA's Brandon Topham's team went in and executed an Anton Piller order the business address in Polokwane, and the Marks' home in Durban. Since then the scheme has collapsed, despite the best of efforts by the Marks'. And Steynberg has left his wife and gone on the run.

We would interview the lead advocate Vaughn vcitor about how the case is unfolding and put in a request to the hawks. We'd also also the FSCA's Brandon Topham. And we can interview anonymous ZA. We have some nice extra information on both of them, great videos etc, and we'll have to put a right of reply in to Steynberg, and potentially his wife Nerina - who is a manager at the polokwane pick n pay.
metadata.Further information: A hacker collective calling itself Anonymous ZA has released explosive details about Mirror Trading International (MTI), stating that at least R4-billion in bitcoin has flowed through the scheme. In response, MTI told MyBroadband the information stems from private member data that was illegally obtained and that it is “inaccurate at best”. Mirror Trading International is a South African registered company offering Forex trading services by using an automated system to trade with the trading pool on behalf of its members. Johann Steynberg is the CEO and founder of MTI, which focuses on Bitcoin trading and promising members a “truly passive income”. According to MTI, it has over 90 000 active members in 177 countries, and its numbers are growing daily. MTI made headlines recently after the Financial Sector Conduct Authority (FSCA) said it was investigating the company. The FSCA said the current business model of MTI requires it to be in possession of a financial service provider licence. “MTI has informed us that they accept clients’ funds in the form of Bitcoin, pool the funds into one trading account on a forex derivate trading platform, and conduct high-frequency trading through the utilisation of a bot,” the FSCA said. If this is being done as described, then this amounts to financial services, hence the licence requirement. However, the FSCA has a much greater concern about MTI’s activities. The company claims to have more than R2.9 billion in clients’ funds in trading accounts, but the FSCA has not been able to conclusively confirm that the funds exist. “Moreover, the returns on the investments claimed by MTI seems far-fetched and unrealistic,” the FSCA said. At the time, MTI said that its bot-trading is able to generate consistent profits of an average of 10% per month. More recently it said it has seen an average return of 0.5% per day. The FSCA recommended that MTI clients request refunds into their own accounts as soon as possible. The Texas State Securities Board has also issued an emergency cease-and-desist order against MTI and accused it of perpetrating fraud through an illegal international multilevel marketing programme. Canada’s Autorité des Marchés Financiers (AMF) has placed MTI on its list of illegal online platforms, issuing a warning that MTI illegally solicits investors. Anonymous ZA publishes information about MTI Anonymous ZA has published financial information about MTI online based on data collected through MTI’s members portal – mymticlub.com. According to Anonymous ZA, it discovered glaring security vulnerabilities in the online systems of MTI, which it exploited to extract information about the inner workings of the scheme. Anonymous ZA said the vulnerability that exposed MTI’s “back office” system was a lack of basic authentication. Any registered member who is logged into the system could view the information of any other member’s account by simply changing a parameter in the URL. “All data was acquired using simple enumeration and scraping techniques on the mymticlub.com site,” stated Anonymous ZA. “No hacks were performed because the lack of basic security did not require it. Just incrementing an id=? parameter on various URLs provided all the data that you see here.” Using this weakness, it was able to glean detailed information about MTI’s system and see the full names, usernames, e-mail addresses, bitcoin balances, and earnings linked to every account. Anonymous ZA then published an anonymised copy of the data, which was current as of 14 September 2020, on a dark web site called MTILeaks. It said the MTI database shows the company has handled over 22,984 bitcoin in member deposits, amounting to over R4 billion. The data shows that members have withdrawn nearly 15,653 bitcoin (close to R2.9 billion), which means the scheme should still have at least 7,331 bitcoin (over R1.3 billion) of members’ capital in its accounts. However, the data also shows that the scheme has allocated almost 9,916 bitcoin (over R1.8 billion) to members in interest and bonuses. This means that MTI must have a minimum of 17,247 bitcoin (over R3.1 billion) to cover the remaining deposits and earnings of all members who have not yet been withdrawn from the scheme. MyBroadband asked MTI CEO Johann Steynberg if the company has that much liquidity and if he could provide MTI’s bitcoin wallet addresses to prove that the company has the assets to cover its obligations. Steynberg did not answer the question in his initial response to MyBroadband. In a subsequent statement to MyBroadband, MTI said it declined to comment.
